subject: Hosted API commit tiers — proposed month-by-month step-up schedule
messages:
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Alexa Johnson <alexa@brightcart.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit tiers — initial pricing framework

Hi Alexa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Based on our conversation about BrightCart's checkout personalization and real-time recommendation flows, I've sketched a simple committed monthly plan that matches the launch ramp you described. Before I bake this into a formal quote, can you confirm expected monthly token volume ranges for the first 6 months and whether you expect Q4 seasonality spikes (~2–3x) on top of that?

High-level proposal (very negotiable):
- Baseline per-token rate (hosted API): $0.000020 / token (list)
- Commit tiers with step-up schedule: 1M tokens/mo initial commit, step-up to 3M/mo by month 4, 5M/mo by month 7 (example)
- Committed discount: 10% at 1M, 18% at 3M, 26% at 5M (applied to per-token list price)
- True-up: monthly reconciliation with overage at committed discounted rate; option to true-up quarterly to allow flexibility
- Ramp credits: one-time launch credit to offset initial churn/beta tokens (can be structured as bill credit)

Attached is a draft pricing-schedule (pricing-schedule-v1.xlsx) that lays out a few variants: conservative ramp, aggressive ramp, and an elastic commit with monthly step increases.

If you can send the expected month-by-month token estimate (even a range), I can produce two options: (A) lower-minimum commit with smaller discounts and (B) a stepped commit with larger discounts but with a 6–12 month minimum term.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0172

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful and a good starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Expected ramp (approx, tokens/month):
  - M1 (pilot): 0.8M tokens
  - M2: 1.5M
  - M3: 2.2M
  - M4 (sitewide soft launch): 4.5M
  - M5: 6.0M
  - M6: 7.5M

2) Seasonality: we have a significant Q4 push for holiday promotions — our simulations show peaks up to ~2.8x baseline in Nov/Dec.

3) Key asks:
  - Can BrightCart structure a step-up commit that allows smaller initial commits (to reduce risk) but guarantees the larger step-ups as the product lands?
  - We prefer monthly true-ups rather than quarterly; however, we're open to a compromise if it improves the discount materially.
  - Any chance to get an onboarding/launch credit for the first two months (to offset instrumentation and tuning cost)?

Tom — looping you in; we'd like to get commercial terms nailed by end of July so legal can move quickly.

Thanks,
Alexa Johnson
Head of Product, BrightCart
alexa@brightcart.com

Appreciate the detail — that's exactly what I needed. Based on your month-by-month estimates, here's a concrete option set that balances flexibility and unit economics. I've attached a draft SOW and updated pricing spreadsheet with exact dollar math.

Option A — Flexible step-up (lower minimum)
- Term: 12 months
- M1–M2 commit: 1M tokens/mo (10% off list)
- M3–M4 commit: 3M tokens/mo (18% off list)
- M5–M12: true-up monthly at committed discounted rate; overages billed monthly
- Onboarding credit: $10k one-time credit (applied to first invoice)
- Early termination: pro-rated true-up to list price for any unused committed tokens if canceled before 6 months

Option B — Aggressive step-up (better pricing)
- Term: 12 months (firm)
- M1 commit: 1M
- Step to 3M in month 4 and 6M in month 7 (step-up milestones required)
- Discounts: 15% @1M, 22% @3M, 30% @6M
- True-up monthly; 60-day ramp credit if volume misses a milestone but demonstrates upward trajectory
- Onboarding credit: $25k if we sign before Aug 1

Notes:
- We can cap Q4 spike handling with a ‘seasonal cushion’ — allow up to 3x committed capacity for two months at the committed discounted rate without moving to a higher commitment tier automatically. That protects you from spikes without penalizing you.
- We generally do monthly true-ups; quarterlies are negotiable if you need runway for invoicing.

Karthik (SE) — I copied you on the SOW for instrumentation and any outstanding product questions. Monica (CS) — can you propose an onboarding plan and timings if BrightCart picks Option B?

If that looks good I can put Option A and B into a formal commercial term sheet for Tom and legal.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi — thanks for laying out both options. A couple of concerns from procurement/finance here:

1) Upfront risk: committing to a 12-month firm term with an aggressive step-up is a lot of upside for Redwood but asymmetric risk for BrightCart if adoption stalls. Do you offer any runway or protection?
2) Can we avoid steep fees for failing to hit a milestone? We'd prefer a soft step with credits rather than penalties.
3) Legal will want a clear early-termination cap and a 30–60 day notice provision.

If Redwood can offer a 90-day runway (credits that convert to committed volume after demonstrated adoption) and soften milestone penalties into a 30% credit (instead of full true-up), we can be much more comfortable. Also, confirm that Q4 seasonality cushion exists in writing.

Thanks — happy to review a stripped-down commercial term sheet (one page) that captures these protections and the economic levers.

Tom
VP Product Operations, BrightCart
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@brightcart.com>, Alexa Johnson <alexa@brightcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit tiers — initial pricing framework

Tom — totally fair asks. I've looped in Marcus from Finance and Karthik from SE to propose language that addresses runway and milestone softness. Summary of revised commercial guardrails: 

- Runway credit: 90-day launch credit (applies as bill credit for shortfall vs committed for months 1–3). If adoption reaches the next milestone within those 90 days, the credit converts into committed volume (no refund).
- Soft milestones: failing a step-up milestone triggers a 30% credit on the shortfall rather than a full true-up to list price.
- Seasonality cushion: firm — allow up to 3x committed capacity for two pre-agreed months (Q4 window) at the committed discounted rate, automatically honored without bumping tier.
- Early termination: cap on termination fee equal to 3 months of committed discounted spend, with 30-day notice.
- Onboarding credit escalation: still valid (up to $25k) if we sign by Aug 1; otherwise $10k.

Marcus — can you confirm any accounting/recognition constraints on converting runway credits to committed volume and whether the onboarding credit needs to be amortized?

Karthik — please confirm the instrumentation plan and an estimated 3-week kickoff window after signature. I'll prepare a one-page commercial term sheet and a redlined contract stub for your legal to review.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi — this looks promising and addresses our main concerns. We have two small asks before we proceed to legal:

1) Add explicit language that Q4 seasonal cushion applies only if BrightCart provides a 30-day forecast before the two months in question (we'll commit to that).
2) Limit the early termination cap to the lower of (a) 3 months committed discounted spend or (b) $150k — our procurement needs a numeric ceiling.

If you can add those tweaks to the one-page term sheet, we're happy to route to legal and aim to sign before Aug 15. Please send the DocuSign-ready agreement and I'll have our GC drop comments directly into DocuSign.

Thanks — excited to move forward.

Best,
Alexa
